title: 2026 AFC South preview
channel_name: The Athletic Football Show: A show about the NFL
text: Once the butt of jokes across the league, the AFC South produced two teams that won at least 12 games last year, and for a time looked like it could get three teams into the playoffs. The Texans and Jaguars return this year as teams with legitimate aspirations to make deep postseason runs, while the Colts and Titans have reason to believe that they could notch the sorts of improvements that would push them to growth in 2026. Can the Texans offense do enough to make the most of an elite defense? Was the Jaguars second-half surge on offense for real? How do the Colts capture the magic from the first half of last season and keep it for a full 17-game slate? And just what would be a successful season for the Titans? Robert Mays, Derrik Klassen and Dave Helman answer those questions, and a whole lot more, on this episode of The Athletic Football Show. title: Why ESPN left Bo Nix out of the top 100 — and what his teammates know BEST | Orange & Blue Today
text: ESPN left Bo Nix out of their Top 100, and Broncos Country is rightfully fired up. The national analysts have never understood Nix — not his command, not his toughness, not the way he elevates the offense. But inside the building, his teammates keep saying the same thing: Bo is different, Bo is steady, and Bo is ready. Is he about to make a year‑three leap like Josh Allen once did. title: Will Josh Jacobs play in 2026 and going inside the mind of fake 49ers player Daejon Love + more!
text: Manish Mehta and Eric Burgess delve into a wild NFL weekend, including a closer look at the three players put on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt list. What’s next for Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold, Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathan Cooper? The guys take a closer look at whether Jacobs will be suspended or play again in 2026? Do the Packers have enough running back depth with MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and recently acquired Kaleb Johnson (from the Pittsburgh Steelers)? The guys move on to discuss the headliners on NFL Cutdown Day highlighted by former Tennessee Titans quarterback Will Levis. The conversation moves to the four teams that decided to keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man rosters: Atlanta Falcons, Minnesota Vikings, Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers. Does Eagles G.M. Howie Roseman really believe in Jalen Hurts? Burg and Manish wrap up talking about the wildest story of the NFL offseason: Fraudster Daejon Love, who pretended to be a San Francisco 49ers player to defraud 26 women out of $1.3 million. Love’s seemingly endless videos have surfaced in recent days. And the guys are amazed by his level of detail to run his scam.
